fluff.overview:
The Brigand holds the dubious distinction of being the first BattleMech ever manufactured by a pirate organization. Introduced in 3065, the twenty-five-ton light 'Mech was cobbled together by Vengeance Incorporated, an arms manufacturer run by the pirates of the Haven Star Cluster under the direction of their leader, the self-styled pirate queen known as "Lady Death" Trevaline. The LDT designation itself is drawn from Trevaline's initials, a brazen signature on what authorities consider an alarming escalation in Periphery pirate capability.

Despite its outlaw origins, the Brigand employs surprisingly advanced construction techniques, all sourced through an extensive network of theft, black market dealings, and graft. Designed from the ground up as a raiding platform, the Brigand prioritizes offensive striking power and mobility over survivability, a philosophy that earned it an immediate and notorious reputation among Periphery border worlds.
fluff.capabilities:
Built on a contraband endo steel chassis and powered by a GM 150 fusion engine, the Brigand achieves a respectable top speed of just over ninety-seven kilometers per hour. Six contraband jump jets provide a one-hundred-eighty-meter jump capability, giving the design excellent tactical flexibility for a raiding 'Mech. The all-energy weapons loadout of two Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers and two Sutel Precision Line medium pulse lasers was a deliberate choice, eliminating ammunition dependency and reducing the logistical burden that plagues most pirate operations. Ten double heat sinks manage the thermal load efficiently, allowing sustained fire without significant performance degradation.

The Brigand's most glaring weakness is its armor protection. With only four tons of Haven Cent armor (the sole locally produced component) the design offers minimal survivability against sustained fire. Worse still, nearly all protection is concentrated on the forward arc, with less than half a ton covering the rear. This was reportedly a deliberate specification to discourage retreat among pirate MechWarriors. While this philosophy keeps raiders aggressive, it means any flanking attack or rear strike is almost certainly fatal. The Brigand's survival depends entirely on its speed, jump capability, and the pilot's willingness to disengage before concentrated fire can be brought to bear.
fluff.history:
The Brigand's origins trace back to the Haven Star Cluster, where Vengeance Incorporated managed the unlikely feat of establishing a functional BattleMech production line from components acquired almost entirely through piracy and black market channels. The design first appeared in 3065, and while authorities initially debated whether the 'Mech's existence was more alarming as a military threat or as evidence of growing pirate organizational capability, the Brigand quickly proved itself a dangerous raiding platform against Taurian Concordat border worlds.

Prior to the Jihad, the majority of Brigands operated with pirate bands based in the Haven Star Cluster, though a handful appeared in the forces of other Periphery raiders including the Band of the Damned, the Tortuga Fusiliers, Shen-sè Tian, and the Marcadia Brothers. The Taurian Concordat bore the brunt of Brigand raids during this period, managing to salvage several examples and destroy others, providing valuable intelligence on the design's capabilities and limitations.

The Brigand's success drew the attention of the Word of Blake during the Jihad, who offered clandestine resources to Vengeance Incorporated to improve both the design and its production capacity. This shadowy partnership resulted in a wave of new variants incorporating increasingly advanced technology, much of it stolen from Taurian and Inner Sphere storehouses. A second production facility was established on Tortuga Prime with Blakist assistance, dramatically expanding the Brigand's manufacturing base.

The full extent of Word of Blake involvement became apparent in 3076 when the Filtvelt Coalition launched a punitive raid against Tortuga Prime. The Thumpers, seeking to strike at both pirate bands and Vengeance Incorporated itself, stumbled upon crude assembly plants concealed within converted warehouses. Five highly advanced prototype Brigands powered up and engaged the Coalition forces in a fierce urban battle. Though the raiders ultimately fled, detailed sensor scans captured enough data for engineers to reconstruct the prototypes' specifications.

The features of these prototypes were ultimately distilled into the LDT-5, which first appeared on Lackland in 3083 and has continued to plague the Filtvelt Coalition and neighboring Periphery realms. Even after the fall of the Word of Blake, Vengeance Incorporated has maintained production at both the Haven Star Cluster and Tortuga Prime facilities, ensuring the Brigand remains a persistent threat across the Periphery.
fluff.deployment: The first of five advanced prototypes discovered during the Filtvelt Coalition's 3076 raid on Tortuga Prime, this variant mounts two medium X-pulse lasers and an SRM-4 missile launcher on the standard Brigand chassis. An extralight engine maintains the base model's speed profile while freeing internal weight for the upgraded weapons package. The combination of accurate pulse fire and short-range missiles gives this prototype a focused close-combat orientation, though its reliance on missile ammunition undermines the logistical independence that defines the Brigand concept.
